Relay note 1A says Olympus governs. The Athena term explains its own role and code-name meanings; the Hermes term does not, and its source lists only S1. findings.evidence: Relay note 1A/2A: Athena is the strategy and learning role within Olympus, and Sri is the owner (Zeus) of Olympus. The test checks only that relation targets exist, not what the relations mean.

summary: The structure is sound. docs/ontology.toml holds the seven seeded terms, each with a definition, a misread, sources that exist and relations to defined terms. The new test file has 10 tests and they pass; its in-memory negative tests cover a missing source, a source that does not exist, a dangling relation and a duplicate term. D109 records the decision and its alternatives. clippy and fmt --check are clean. No email address or secret appears. But the Hermes entry is wrong in the way an ontology exists to prevent. It defines Hermes only as Hermes Agent, "a studied system, not part of Athena". The Project Olympus brief, which governs (BRIEF.md line 597, Pantheon table), names Hermes as Olympus's Orchestration god. The Athena entry explains its own two meanings and Hermes does not, so an agent reading the file would misread the word Hermes in Olympus text. I rate this major, so the verdict is fail. The fix is small: define both meanings (the Pantheon role and the studied Hermes Agent) and cite BRIEF.md#2. The Pantheon next to the S1 source.
